Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can include with the RFP; happy to expand any section or hop on a call. I’ve also attached a small example manifest showing how we structure signed artifacts (signed-manifest-example.json).

Overview (high-level):
- Delivery: We publish release artifacts as OCI images + a companion signed manifest that lists image digests, SBOM link, and artifact metadata. For air-gapped sites we provide an offline image bundle (tarball) and/or an "airgap registry" export tar that can be imported into an on-prem registry (Harbor/Artifactory). Transport is customer-managed (SFTP, physical media).

- Signing model: We sign the manifest and image digests using an industry-standard container signing tool (we currently publish with cosign). Customers may: 1) use Redwood-managed signing keys, 2) upload and register a customer key (recommended for audits), or 3) integrate an HSM-backed key via our PKCS#11 plugin. All signatures are timestamped and included in the manifest.

- Incremental patches/updates: We support delta bundles (layer-based diffs) and full image bundles. For air-gapped installs, customers can apply either: a) periodic incremental bundle (recommended for smaller bandwidth) or b) full update bundle. Each bundle includes a signed manifest with the new digests and a migration checklist.

- Reproducible builds & chain-of-custody: Every release contains an SBOM (CycloneDX), build commit hash, builder environment notes, and a PGP-signed build provenance file. We retain CI build logs and can export a signed provenance package as evidence for audits.

- Hardware & attestation: We recommend either: a) customer HSM (recommended) with a registered public key in Redwood control plane, or b) a FIPS-validated HSM appliance at the customer site for private key storage. For attestation we support integration with TPM-based node attestation for runtime hosts.

Actionable next steps (proposed):
- Confirm whether Acuity wants Redwood-managed signing or customer-owned key + HSM.
- Decide preferred transport (SFTP vs physical ship).
- Schedule a 45-minute technical workshop with our security engineer (Marcus) and your infra lead to validate the import/import validation flow.

Cc’ing Marcus to propose the checklist for key rotation and verification.

Thanks —

Hey team — quick note from the offline tooling side (Offline Images Inc.). We provide an offline registry export/import agent that works with Redwood’s export tar format (checksums + signature bundle). Our recommended pattern:

- Export: produce an "artifact bundle" containing OCI images (.tar), signed manifest (cosign + timestamp), and SBOMs.
- Transport: deliver via encrypted external drive or pre-authorized SFTP with checksums + signature file.
- Import: local operator verifies cosign signatures (or PGP), validates SBOM, and imports to local Harbor. Our agent can perform these checks and provide an import log for audits.

If helpful I can share our import-agent doc and a short checklist we hand to customers. Happy to join the workshop.

Sara / team — adding a security checklist and a few clarifications from our side (short bullets you can attach to the RFP).

Security checklist (suggested minimum):
- Key control: Customer HSM or Redwood HSM with customer-managed keys. Provide key rotation window and emergency revocation steps.
- Signature verification: Verification must include both cosign signature validation and digest match; require timestamp authority verification for time-of-signing.
- SBOM validation: Scan SBOMs offline against approved policy; preserve scan results in the import log.
- Immutable manifests: Sign manifests at release time; do not allow unsigned manifest acceptance in air-gapped mode.
- Audit logs: Import tool must produce tamper-evident logs (signed import record) including operator identity, checksums, and verification results.
- Rollback policy: Each bundle includes a rollback manifest and a validated test plan; recommend a staged roll-forward with a canary host when feasible.

Operational notes:
- We should agree on who holds the primary signing key for production releases. For audit-friendliness, customer-owned key + HSM is preferred.
- For emergency hotfixes we provide a signed emergency bundle; the customer’s import process must require an emergency justification note that is logged and signed by the operator.

I can prepare a one-page HSM integration appendix (PKCS#11 examples, suggested rotation policy).

-Marcus
